correctness.rationale: A bijection plus cycle lemma gives exact uniform composition profiles; marking a fixed vector of rare blocks gives the displayed all-n mixed factorial moments. Conditional on these Palm markings, the number of positive remaining entries is 1 plus a hypergeometric variable with both success and sample fractions approaching 1/2, so a standard hypergeometric central limit theorem preserves the global Gaussian fluctuation. Mixed factorial moments with Gaussian test functions and Poisson determinacy yield joint independence. A uniform n*2^{-r} expected-count bound transfers finite-window independence to the largest block. Every quantifier and lattice subsequence is explicit. The standalone checker passed 824 integer/rational finite assertions and 6 numerical scale comparisons; the limit is analytically proved, not inferred from enumeration.

value.rationale: The interaction of the global square-root block-count fluctuations and logarithmic rare-block extremes is an intrinsically motivated question for canonical Catalan random structures. Prior separate marginals leave their dependence unresolved. The result identifies a full finite rare-block Poisson vector independent of the Gaussian global statistic, with a natural largest-block corollary; the combinatorial Palm/hypergeometric mechanism explains the structural decoupling rather than merely computing an arbitrary invariant.
